title: The Latest Crier for Apr 26, 2026

Joe B's Last Calm & Senior Night

Join us for Joe B's Last Calm on May 3 in the Upper Chapel at 6:30 pm. Let's celebrate his 26 years of faithful ministry & the graduating class of '26. We will worship, hear a teaching from Joe B, & enjoy time together eating caramel bars after. All alumni, students, faculty, & staff are invited. Please RSVP so we know #'s for treats! 
Last Calm & Senior Night RSVP: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eJ_97JlTMaQZQSfP7cpsp43n8bN2YHajYWHo082uoYY/edit?usp=sharing 

Joe B Photos: https://photos.app.goo.gl/CdfxYg2ep4Q9zriS6 

Thank you Joe: https://forms.gle/HSeZ8hJBe9psBR6Y6

Grad School Workshop in Maytag's Van Emmerik Studio!

On Tuesday, 4/28, at 11 am in the Van Emmerik Studio, Jeremy Burke will lead a Grad School Workshop. We'll begin by going over the general process for developing into a competitive applicant for most graduate programs. After that, each attendee may review the website of a graduate program they might consider and we'll work together to address any questions that arise. This is a great introduction to the grad school process. If you think graduate school might be in your future, or you're just curious about learning more, we hope to see you there!

Campus Wide Worship & Baptism NIGHT

FCA, InterVarsity, ALIVE, & Campus Ministries are hosting a Worship & Baptism Night on May 10 at 8:00 pm in the Chapel! Come for worship, student testimonies, & snacks to follow. If you would like to take this step in your faith & be baptized, reach out to Joe ( brummelj@central.edu ) or Hannah ( laflinh@central.edu ) in the Lower Chapel. We hope to see you there!

Out of the Darkness Walk

Please join us May 3rd in Maytag, 12pm support fair, 1:15pm Speakers, once the speakers are done then the walk will start. 
We’re hosting the Out of the Darkness Walk in partnership with The American Foundation for Suicide Prevention (AFSP), and it’s centered around raising awareness, breaking stigma, and reminding people that they are not alone. At a place like Central, it’s easy to feel like everyone has it together, but the reality is that there are people carrying things that we don’t know about. Whether it is stress, anxiety, loneliness, or deeper struggles, suicide prevention starts with creating a space where people feel seen, supported, and not alone. If you have any questions please email: carstensk2@central.edu
